\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{பின்னடைவு} (piṉṉaṭaivu)}{பின்னடைவு (piṉṉaṭaivu)}]{\ta{பின்னடைவு} (piṉṉaṭaivu) — a setback}

\label{lesson:TA-C546-pinnataivu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for considerably, then the Tamil for a model.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{பின்னடைவு}}
\textbf{\ta{பின்னடைவு}} — \emph{piṉṉaṭaivu} — \textquotedblleft{}a setback\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{மழை} \ta{பெய்தால்} \ta{கட்டட} \ta{வேலைக்குப்} \ta{பின்னடைவு} \ta{ஏற்படும்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maḻai peytāl kaṭṭaṭa vēlaikkup piṉṉaṭaivu ēṟpaṭum.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If it rains, the building work will suffer a setback.
\end{quote}

What suffers it takes -\ta{க்கு}: \ta{வேலைக்குப்} \ta{பின்னடைவு}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{பின்னடைவு}} (\emph{piṉṉaṭaivu}) is a native compound: \ta{பின்} (\emph{piṉ}), \textquotedblleft{}back, behind\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 4205), and \ta{அடைவு} (\emph{aṭaivu}), \textquotedblleft{}reaching, getting\textquotedblright{}: a going back.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{piṉṉaṭaivu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{piṉṉaṭaivu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maḻai peytāl kaṭṭaṭa vēlaikkup piṉṉaṭaivu ēṟpaṭum.} — If it rains, the building work will suffer a setback.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for considerably, then the Tamil for a model, then say \emph{piṉṉaṭaivu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{பின்னடைவு} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A setback\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{இடையூறு} (iṭaiyūṟu)}{இடையூறு (iṭaiyūṟu)}]{\ta{இடையூறு} (iṭaiyūṟu) — a hindrance; a disturbance}

\label{lesson:TA-C546-itaiyuru}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a model, then the Tamil for a setback.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{இடையூறு}}
\textbf{\ta{இடையூறு}} — \emph{iṭaiyūṟu} — \textquotedblleft{}a hindrance; a disturbance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{சத்தம்} \ta{என்} \ta{படிப்புக்கு} \ta{இடையூறாக} \ta{இருக்கிறது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{cattam eṉ paṭippukku iṭaiyūṟāka irukkiṟatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The noise is a disturbance to my studies.
\end{quote}

With -\ta{ஆக} \ta{இரு} it says something gets in the way: \ta{இடையூறாக} \ta{இரு}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{இடையூறு}} (\emph{iṭaiyūṟu}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 435 gives \ta{இடையூறு} (\emph{iṭaiyūṟu}), \textquotedblleft{}an obstacle\textquotedblright{}, beside \ta{இடர்}, \textquotedblleft{}trouble\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṭaiyūṟu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṭaiyūṟu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cattam eṉ paṭippukku iṭaiyūṟāka irukkiṟatu.} — The noise is a disturbance to my studies.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a model, then the Tamil for a setback, then say \emph{iṭaiyūṟu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{இடையூறு} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A hindrance; a disturbance\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{குறுக்கீடு} (kuṟukkīṭu)}{குறுக்கீடு (kuṟukkīṭu)}]{\ta{குறுக்கீடு} (kuṟukkīṭu) — an interruption; an interference}

\label{lesson:TA-C546-kurukkitu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a setback, then the Tamil for a hindrance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{குறுக்கீடு}}
\textbf{\ta{குறுக்கீடு}} — \emph{kuṟukkīṭu} — \textquotedblleft{}an interruption; an interference\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{பேச்சின்} \ta{நடுவில்} \ta{யாரும்} \ta{குறுக்கீடு} \ta{செய்யவில்லை}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pēcciṉ naṭuvil yārum kuṟukkīṭu ceyyavillai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Nobody interrupted in the middle of the speech.
\end{quote}

With \ta{செய்} (\emph{cey}) it becomes a verb: \ta{குறுக்கீடு} \ta{செய்}, to interrupt.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{குறுக்கீடு}} (\emph{kuṟukkīṭu}) is a native compound: \ta{குறுக்கு} (\emph{kuṟukku}), \textquotedblleft{}across, crosswise\textquotedblright{}, from \ta{குறு}, \textquotedblleft{}short\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1851), with the noun ending \emph{-īṭu}: something put across the way.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kuṟukkīṭu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kuṟukkīṭu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pēcciṉ naṭuvil yārum kuṟukkīṭu ceyyavillai.} — Nobody interrupted in the middle of the speech.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a setback, then the Tamil for a hindrance, then say \emph{kuṟukkīṭu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{முட்டுக்கட்டை} (muṭṭukkaṭṭai)}{முட்டுக்கட்டை (muṭṭukkaṭṭai)}]{\ta{முட்டுக்கட்டை} (muṭṭukkaṭṭai) — a stumbling block}

\label{lesson:TA-C546-muttukkattai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a hindrance, then the Tamil for an interruption.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{முட்டுக்கட்டை}}
\textbf{\ta{முட்டுக்கட்டை}} — \emph{muṭṭukkaṭṭai} — \textquotedblleft{}a stumbling block\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{பணப்} \ta{பற்றாக்குறை} \ta{திட்டத்துக்கு} \ta{முட்டுக்கட்டையாக} \ta{இருக்கிறது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{paṇap paṟṟākkuṟai tiṭṭattukku muṭṭukkaṭṭaiyāka irukkiṟatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shortage of money is a stumbling block for the plan.
\end{quote}

Word for word \textquotedblleft{}a prop-log\textquotedblright{}, a block put under a wheel to stop it.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{முட்டுக்கட்டை}} (\emph{muṭṭukkaṭṭai}) is a native compound: \ta{முட்டு} (\emph{muṭṭu}), \textquotedblleft{}a hindrance, an obstacle\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 4933), and \ta{கட்டை} (\emph{kaṭṭai}), \textquotedblleft{}a log, a block\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muṭṭukkaṭṭai}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muṭṭukkaṭṭai}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paṇap paṟṟākkuṟai tiṭṭattukku muṭṭukkaṭṭaiyāka irukkiṟatu.} — The shortage of money is a stumbling block for the plan.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a hindrance, then the Tamil for an interruption, then say \emph{muṭṭukkaṭṭai} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{முட்டுக்கட்டை} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A stumbling block\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{தாக்குப்பிடி} (tākkuppiṭi)}{தாக்குப்பிடி (tākkuppiṭi)}]{\ta{தாக்குப்பிடி} (tākkuppiṭi) — to hold out; to withstand}

\label{lesson:TA-C546-takkuppiti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for an interruption, then the Tamil for a stumbling block.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{தாக்குப்பிடி}}
\textbf{\ta{தாக்குப்பிடி}} — \emph{tākkuppiṭi} — \textquotedblleft{}to hold out; to withstand\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{இந்தப்} \ta{பழைய} \ta{பாலம்} \ta{அடுத்த} \ta{வெள்ளத்தில்} \ta{தாக்குப்பிடிக்குமா}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{intap paḻaiya pālam aṭutta veḷḷattil tākkuppiṭikkumā?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Will this old bridge hold out in the next flood?
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{தாக்குப்பிடித்தேன்}, \emph{tākkuppiṭittēṉ}.

Usually with a thing as subject, in the future or with \ta{முடியும்}: \ta{தாக்குப்பிடிக்க} \ta{முடியாது}, it cannot hold out.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{தாக்குப்பிடி}} (\emph{tākkuppiṭi}) is a native compound: \ta{தாக்கு} (\emph{tākku}), \textquotedblleft{}a blow, an attack\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 3150), and \ta{பிடி} (\emph{piṭi}), \textquotedblleft{}to hold\textquotedblright{}: to hold against the blow.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tākkuppiṭi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intap paḻaiya pālam aṭutta veḷḷattil tākkuppiṭikkumā?} — Will this old bridge hold out in the next flood?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for an interruption, then the Tamil for a stumbling block, then say \emph{tākkuppiṭi} again
\end{itemize}
